mcqs.question: A view creates its own instance of an ObservableObject view model directly in its body, and marks it @ObservedObject. What bug does this risk?
options: The view model can be recreated on every re-render, silently resetting state that should have persisted
@Published properties on the view model stop firing objectWillChange entirely
The view model leaks because @ObservedObject retains it strongly forever
There is no bug — @StateObject and @ObservedObject behave identically for views that create their own instance
mcqs.explanation: @ObservedObject doesn't take ownership of the instance's lifetime; if the view creates the object itself, a re-render can recreate a fresh instance, resetting state. @StateObject is specifically for the case where the view owns and creates the instance, ensuring it persists across re-renders.

mcqs.question: You need a form's submit button enabled only once both a username field and a password field have non-empty values. Which Combine operator combination fits best?
options: map on each publisher individually, applied in sequence
combineLatest on the two publishers, then map the pair to a boolean and filter empty values along the way
debounce on each field to wait for typing to stop, with no further operators needed
removeDuplicates on a single merged publisher
mcqs.explanation: combineLatest is built exactly for merging two independent publishers and reacting whenever either produces a new value paired with the other's latest — the right shape for validating two fields together. debounce alone doesn't combine two separate publishers, and map alone can't merge two streams into one.

mcqs.question: In a debounced search pipeline, the sink closure captures self strongly instead of using [weak self]. What's the consequence?
options: The search results stop updating after the first debounce fires
Nothing — sink closures are always weak by default in Combine
The view model can never deallocate, since the subscription it owns holds a strong reference back to itself
The debounce timer resets on every keystroke instead of collapsing them
mcqs.explanation: The view model stores the subscription, and if the subscription's closure captures the view model strongly too, that's a cycle: the object can never be released because it's indirectly keeping itself alive through its own stored subscription. Combine closures are not weak by default; that's an explicit choice via [weak self].

mcqs.question: A view reads only cart.total from a view model that also has an items array. Under ObservableObject with @Published on both properties, versus @Observable, when does this view re-render?
options: Under both, only when total changes
Under ObservableObject, whenever either items or total changes; under @Observable, only when total changes
Under @Observable, whenever either property changes, since it tracks the whole object
Under both, whenever either property changes, since SwiftUI can't distinguish reads at the property level
mcqs.explanation: ObservableObject's objectWillChange fires on any @Published mutation regardless of what a given view actually reads, causing over-rendering; @Observable tracks which properties a view's body actually accesses and only triggers a re-render for changes to those specific properties.

mcqs.question: A call to $query.sink { ... } is made without storing its return value anywhere. What happens to the subscription?
options: It is cancelled almost immediately, since the returned AnyCancellable token owns the subscription and nothing retains it
It runs for the lifetime of the app regardless of whether the token is stored
Combine automatically stores it in a global registry for you
It throws a runtime error the first time query changes
mcqs.explanation: The AnyCancellable returned by sink is what keeps the subscription alive; if it's discarded immediately with nothing holding a reference, Combine cancels the subscription right away. There's no automatic global registry, and this doesn't crash — it just silently does nothing.

mcqs.question: A view model marks an internal retry counter (never displayed in any view) as @Published, and it increments frequently. What's the practical effect?
options: No effect, since @Published only triggers re-renders for properties a view actually binds to in its layout
The retry counter itself silently fails to update because @Published requires the property to be read by at least one view
It's a compile-time error, since @Published requires the property to be observed by a view
Every mutation fires objectWillChange, triggering a re-render check on every view observing the object, even ones that never read that counter
mcqs.explanation: Under ObservableObject, objectWillChange fires on any @Published mutation regardless of whether any view actually displays that property, so frequent internal churn can trigger unnecessary re-render checks across every observing view. This is exactly the over-render pattern that @Observable's per-property tracking fixes.
